**STEP 1 - Scene:** A single whole apple (red-and-yellow variety) on a white square plate. It is a snack, not a meal.

**STEP 2 - Vessel:** A square white plate, about 22 cm across. Using a round-equivalent diameter of 22 cm, area = 3.14 x 11² ≈ 380 cm². No other food is on the plate.

**STEP 3 - Items:** One whole apple. No oil, dressing, or sauce is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The apple's footprint is about 8 cm across, roughly 50 cm², or about 13% of the plate area.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Treating the whole apple as a sphere of about 8 cm diameter gives about 270 ml. The flat-footprint envelope method (50 cm² x 7.5 cm ≈ 375 ml) overstates a rounded whole fruit, so I use the sphere volume.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Whole fruit is much denser than a loose pile of cut pieces. I use about 0.7 g/ml: 270 ml x 0.7 ≈ 190 g. This is close to a typical medium apple (about 150-180 g).

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Raw apple is about 52 kcal/100 g. 190 g x 0.52 ≈ 99 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** A single medium apple at about 190 g and about 100 kcal is plausible for the visible item. A fully covered dinner plate would hold several hundred grams, which is not the case here.
